title: Respond, Recover, Review: Incident Playbook and Game Day Syllabus
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document describes a single, opinionated lifecycle for incidents at Redwood: Respond → Recover → Review. It consolidates triage ladders, step-by-step containment and recovery runbooks, a postmortem template, on-call rotation rules, and a reproducible game day syllabus for team readiness. Use this as the canonical operational path for any incident affecting customer-facing inference services or control plane components.

Scope
- Applies to all production incidents impacting Redwood-hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private control plane services.
- Excludes non-prod test environments (see team wiki for staging incident guidance).

Quick definitions
- Incident: any event causing customer-visible degradation, increased error rates, latency SLO breaches, or data integrity issues.
- Major incident: multi-region outage, sustained latency SLO violations >30m, or data loss.
- Bridge: primary coordination channel (Slack #inc-bridge by default).

Roles & ownership
1) Incident Commander (IC): owns triage decisions, public comms, and rollback choices. Usually senior SRE or on-call service owner.
2) Bridge Operator: runs the bridge, collects evidence, and creates updates. Typically the on-call SRE.
3) Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): runtime, networking, database, billing, security.
4) Customer Liaison: customer-success engineer for customer-impacted incidents.
5) Postmortem Author: the person who documents the timeline and actions within 72 hours.

Triage decision ladder (first 15 minutes)
1) Detect: alert fires or customer report.
2) Acknowledge: on-call sets initial status in the bridge within 5 minutes.
3) Classify: apply the impact matrix (below) and decide major vs minor.
4) IC assignment: if major, escalate to IC immediately; if minor, on-call handles.
5) Stabilize: execute containment runbook snippets.

Impact matrix (short)
| Customer Impact | Traffic impact | SLO impact | Classification |
|-----------------|----------------|------------|----------------|
| Single customer, degraded responses | <1% traffic | None/very small | P2 |
| Multiple customers, increased latency | 1-10% traffic | SLO at risk | P1 |
| Widespread errors or region down | >10% | SLO breach | Major/P0 |

Immediate containment runbook (first 30 minutes)
1) Put a short-status placeholder: "Investigation underway; initial mitigation in progress."
2) Turn off automated scaling/burst if it's causing churn (CLI: redwood infra scale --service <svc> --mode paused).
3) Apply quick-filters: route new traffic to fallback model variant or healthy region per routing policy. Example: set routing policy via console -> Traffic -> Fallback: small-model-v1.
4) If CPU/GPU exhaustion: evict long-running jobs and enable preemptible fallback pools. Command sample: kubectl cordon <node> && redwood node-drain --evict-long-kv --force.
5) If memory leakage suspected: restart the service with crash-loop protection removed: systemctl restart redwood-runtime-<svc> or k roll restart <deployment>.

Evidence & data collection checklist
- Timestamped alert bindings (incident open time)
- Grafana dashboards: latency-by-route, token-throughput, GPU-utilization, queue-depth
- Recent deployments and rollouts (git commit hashes, canary IDs)
- Error traces and most frequent exceptions
- Customer reports and sample request IDs

Mitigation -> Recovery (30m–4h)
1) Confirm root cause hypothesis with focused tests (run replay on canary).
2) If workaround available (e.g., rollback to previous build or pin to non-quantized model), implement with a canary and 10% traffic test.
3) Monitor for regression for at least two SLO windows (typical windows: 1m/5m/1h depending on metric).
4) If fix is code-level, create a hotfix branch, CI run, and deploy via canary. Tag changelog with incident ID.
5) When stable for recovery SLOs, prepare rollback of temporary mitigations.

Communication templates
- Internal bridge update (concise):
  [HH:MM UTC] STATUS: Investigating | IMPACT: region us-west high latency | ACTION: routing fallback enabled to us-east | OWNER: @oncall-sre | NEXT: 15m update

- Customer status (public/private):
  Subject: Incident [INC-<id>] - Latency degradation affecting inference API

  Hi <CustomerName>,

  We're actively investigating an issue causing increased latency for text-generation requests in us-west. Our on-call team has enabled automatic routing to alternate regions and a fallback model to reduce impact. We will provide the next update by <ETA 15m>.

  What we're doing: diverting traffic, monitoring failover, validating results.
  What you can expect: service restored for most requests within 30-60 minutes; a follow-up report will be sent when the cause is identified.

  Incident ID: INC-<id>

  Regards,
  Redwood Inference Operations

- Status page template (short):
  Title: Partial outage: inference API (us-west)
  Impact: Increased latency; some requests may time out
  Update: Investigating; fallback routing applied
  Next update: in 15 minutes

Postmortem template (to publish within 72 hours)
1) Title: Postmortem - INC-<id> - one-line summary
2) Severity: P0/P1/P2
3) Date opened / closed / duration
4) Services affected and customer impact (list customers if high impact)
5) Timeline (table of events with HH:MM UTC, actor, action, outcome)
6) Root cause analysis (clear technical narrative)
7) Mitigations implemented during incident (short-term)
8) Permanent remediation and owners (action, target date)
9) Detection gaps and monitoring improvements
10) Communication review (what worked, what didn't)
11) Follow-ups and acceptance criteria for closure
12) Links to evidence (dashboards, logs, commits)

On-call rotation & handoff rules
- Shift length: 1 week primary (Mon 09:00 UTC -> next Mon 09:00 UTC) for SREs; 4-week rotation for on-call leads.
- Swap policy: swaps must be posted to #oncall-swaps and acknowledged by the replacing engineer at least 24 hours prior.
- Handoff checklist (to be filled in Slack or Handoff doc):
  - Current active incidents (IDs and short status)
  - Outstanding action items with owners
  - Known risky changes scheduled in next 24h (deploys, infra changes)
  - Personal contact preference and escalation path

Game day syllabus (90–120 minutes; bi-quarterly)
Purpose: exercise the full Respond→Recover→Review flow under controlled conditions. Rotate inject owners across teams.

1) Pre-work (30m):
   - 5m brief: objectives and scale of injected failure
   - 10m runbook review: triage ladder & containment runbook reviewed by IC
   - 15m environment prep: pre-populated incidents, synthetic traffic, and test telemetry enabled

2) Active exercise (45–60m):
   - Inject: simulate throttling of control-plane API + region CPU spike
   - Observe: on-call detects via alert and opens bridge (goal: <5m)
   - Respond: assign IC, run containment steps, and roll fallback routing
   - Recover: perform targeted rollback or config change; validate with synthetic transactions

3) Debrief and scoring (20–30m):
   - Runbook adherence (0-10): extent to which steps were followed
   - Communication clarity (0-10): clarity and cadence of updates
   - Time-to-detect, time-to-ack, and time-to-recover metrics captured
   - Improvement actions captured as JIRA tickets tagged game-day/<date>

Game day evaluation rubric (examples)
- Detection (0-5): alert fired and was noticed within 5m (5pts).
- Role clarity (0-5): IC and bridge operator were assigned within 3m (5pts).
- Containment effectiveness (0-10): mitigation reduced customer error rate by >75% in one SLO window (10pts).
- Recovery correctness (0-10): rollback or patch restored service without data loss (10pts).
- Communication (0-5): internal and customer message templates used correctly (5pts).

Runbook governance & change control
- Owners: every runbook must list a primary owner and at least one reviewer.
- Review cadence: owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any relevant production change.
- Versioning: runbook edits must include changelog entry and incident tags when used in a real event.

Operational dashboards & useful queries
- Main dashboards: Service Overview, Latency by Route, Model Token Cost, GPU Utilization, Queue Depth.
- Useful queries (examples):
  - Top error types: SELECT error, count(*) FROM logs WHERE service='inference' AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY error LIMIT 20
  - 95th latency by route: grafana/latency?panel=95p-by-route

Appendix: SLOs and escalation thresholds
| Service | SLO (p95) | Warning threshold | Escalation threshold |
|---------|----------:|------------------:|---------------------:|
| Text-generation API | 200ms | 120% of SLO for 10m | 150% of SLO for 5m |
| Embeddings API | 150ms | 120% for 10m | 150% for 5m |
| Control plane API | 100ms | 120% for 10m | 150% for 3m |

Escalation matrix (summary)
- P2: notify team slack + on-call (no IC)
- P1: IC assigned, bridge opened, customer liaison notified
- P0 (major): Exec notif (paging), incident war room, external status page update every 15m

Document maintenance
- Owner: Asha Patel (eng-sre)
- Review cycle: annual mandatory review; otherwise update after any game day or major incident.
